lisa_gravitational_wave_exoplanet_detect.headline: LISA Could Spot Exoplanets Around Double White Dwarfs via Gravitational Waves
lisa_gravitational_wave_exoplanet_detect.summary: New theoretical work shows LISA may detect planets orbiting double white dwarf binaries by measuring Doppler shifts in their gravitational‑wave signals.
highlights: LISA’s triangular spacecraft will sense tiny distance changes to capture continuous waves from ~10,000 double white dwarf systems
The proposed gravitational‑wave radial velocity (GWRV) method could reveal planets as small as 0.5 Jupiter masses
JWST infrared excess and Gaia astrometry could confirm candidate planets out to ~500 light‑years
The approach targets post‑main‑sequence binaries, a regime largely inaccessible to traditional exoplanet surveys

galactic_shock_wave_star_formation.headline: Galactic Shock Wave Reveals Hidden Star Factory in Milky Way Bar
galactic_shock_wave_star_formation.summary: New Nature Astronomy study shows the Milky Way’s rotating bar generates shock fronts that compress gas, igniting star formation where other galaxies suppress it.
highlights: Massive rotating bar extends ~4.3 kiloparsecs (≈14,000 light‑years) from the galactic centre.
Shock fronts along the bar compress gas, triggering massive star formation.
Maser positions align with simulated shock fronts, suggesting the Norma arm is actually a bar‑driven star‑forming region.
Findings challenge the conventional map of the Milky Way and constrain bar length, orientation, and rotation speed.

strain_resistance_jump_magic_angle_graph.headline: Strain Amplifies Resistance Hundred‑Fold in Magic‑Angle Graphene
strain_resistance_jump_magic_angle_graph.summary: Using a piezoelectric silicon strain gauge, researchers found that a 1% stretch of magic‑angle graphene changes its resistance by a factor of one hundred.
highlights: Resistance sensitivity reaches a gauge factor of ~100 at the charge neutrality point.
Strain acts like a magnetic field, scaling the superconducting critical temperature similarly to iron‑based superconductors.
The experiment stacks graphene, hBN, and graphite on piezoelectric silicon wafers for in‑situ strain control.
Findings open a path to probe correlated electron behavior in other 2D semiconductors.

new_viruses_missing_link_evolution.headline: Newly Discovered Viruses Bridge Evolutionary Gap Between HK97-Fold Viruses and Encapsulins
new_viruses_missing_link_evolution.summary: Researchers at University of Miami used AI to uncover tiny viruses that act as evolutionary intermediates linking HK97-fold viral capsids and cellular encapsulin compartments.
highlights: The study identified previously unknown viruses with simple genomes that possess both viral and encapsulin features.
AI tools like AlphaFold and protein language models scanned billions of sequences in the IMG/M database to find the candidates.
The authors propose procapsids as a bidirectional evolutionary bridge between viral capsids and encapsulin shells.
Findings challenge the long‑standing view that encapsulins originated solely from viruses, suggesting repeated mutual evolution.

chaotic_supernova_ejecta.headline: JWST Uncovers Shell Mergers in Cassiopeia A Supernova Remnant
chaotic_supernova_ejecta.summary: Using JWST’s MIRI/MRS, researchers mapped dust in Cassiopeia A, identifying distinct grain types that reveal pre‑explosion shell mergers in the progenitor star.
highlights: Mid‑IR spectra isolate dust from individual arcsecond‑scale clumps, showing SiO₂ dominance in reverse‑shocked ejecta (P1).
Mg₂SiO₄ grains trace circumstellar material in the ‘Green Monster’ region (P2), distinct from progenitor dust.
Ne‑rich carbon dust in P3 indicates a carbon‑oxygen shell merger before core collapse.
JWST resolution surpasses Spitzer, enabling spatially resolved chemistry across the remnant.

stellar_eruption_mira_magnetic_fields.headline: Magnetic Eruption on Mira Star Reveals New Driver of Cosmic Dust
stellar_eruption_mira_magnetic_fields.summary: Astronomers using ALMA have observed a giant magnetic flare on the AGB star Mira, showing magnetic fields can power mass loss alongside radiation pressure.
highlights: The flare created a loop of gas extending out to Saturn‑like distances around Mira
SiO masers in the loop were strongly polarized, mapping the star’s magnetic field geometry
Observations span a decade, the longest detailed study of any non‑solar star
The findings challenge the long‑standing dust‑driven wind model for AGB mass loss

star_final_heartbeat.headline: ALMA Captures Dying Star’s Final Nuclear Pulse, Redefining Sun’s Death
star_final_heartbeat.summary: Using ALMA, astronomers imaged a half‑light‑year gas shell from IRAS 06530‑0213, revealing the star’s last thermal pulse and challenging models of solar‑like death.
highlights: The gas shell spans about half a light‑year and was ejected roughly 6,500 years ago.
Mass‑loss rates dropped for ~2,000 years then surged over the next 1,000 years, shaping filamentary structures.
Spiral‑shaped filaments suggest an unseen companion influencing the ejected material.
Heavy isotopes of carbon, oxygen and nitrogen were detected, contrary to existing nucleosynthesis predictions.

ancient_moon_rocks_far_side_2026.institution: Various (research teams cited in ScienceDaily article)
ancient_moon_rocks_far_side_2026.headline: Moon’s Far‑Side Rocks Reveal Gradual Decline in Asteroid Bombardment
ancient_moon_rocks_far_side_2026.summary: Analysis of Chang’e‑6 impact melt rocks shows asteroid collisions waned over three billion years, challenging the notion of a single cataclysmic bombardment.
highlights: Impact melt ages span from ~4.33 billion to ~1.13 billion years ago
40Ar/39Ar geochronology indicates a steady decrease in impact frequency
Far‑side samples provide a cleaner record than near‑side material
Findings reshape models of early Solar System dynamics

quantum_error_correction_record.headline: Quantinuum's Helios Sets Record Low Error Rate in Quantum Memory
quantum_error_correction_record.summary: The 98‑qubit Helios trapped‑ion processor achieved a 0.0005% failure rate, marking a hundred‑fold improvement over previous benchmarks and edging fault‑tolerant quantum computing nearer.
highlights: Helios recorded just five uncorrectable errors per million rounds, a 0.0005% failure rate.
This surpasses Google Willow’s 0.0772% error rate from its 105‑qubit chip.
Error‑correcting code distance 7 reduced uncorrectable errors by roughly twelve‑fold.
The new technique of leakage repumping uses split‑second laser pulses to restore qubit states.

hidden_planet_beyond_neptune.headline: New Simulations Suggest Small Earth‑Mass Planet Could Hide Beyond Neptune
hidden_planet_beyond_neptune.summary: Computer models published in MNRAS indicate a planet 1.5–2 × Earth’s mass orbiting 350–500 AU could explain the odd trajectories of distant icy bodies.
highlights: The peer‑reviewed study was released on November 23 2026 in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.
Simulations show a planet only 1.5–2 × Earth’s mass could reproduce several unusual orbits of trans‑Neptunian objects such as
The proposed Planet X2 would have an elliptical orbit averaging 350–500 AU, with perihelion no closer than 200 AU.
The Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s Legacy Survey of Space and Time may provide observational tests for the hypothesis.

quantum_diamond_microscopy_semiconductor.headline: Quantum Diamond Microscopy Enables 3D Imaging of Semiconductor Currents
quantum_diamond_microscopy_semiconductor.summary: QuantumDiamonds’ nitrogen‑vacancy sensors now visualize hidden electrical pathways inside 3D semiconductor devices, aiding failure analysis and security checks.
highlights: Spin states of nitrogen‑vacancy defects detect magnetic fields with nanoscale precision
System can map current flow deep within complex 3D chips
Technology supports production‑line inspection and side‑channel vulnerability detection
Company grew from a 2022 Technical University of Munich spin‑out to ~80 staff worldwide

galaxy_killing_wind.headline: Supernova‑driven wind caught quenching star formation in early galaxy CRISTAL‑02
galaxy_killing_wind.summary: Astronomers using JWST and ALMA have observed a fast‑moving gas plume that appears to halt star formation in a massive galaxy just 1.1 billion years after the Big Bang.
highlights: CRISTAL‑02 shows a cold‑gas plume moving at ~100 km s⁻¹, twice its star‑formation rate
No active galactic nucleus detected, indicating supernovae as the wind’s energy source
If the outflow continues, the galaxy could become quiescent in under 50 million years

close_up_images_reveal_giant_dart_impact.headline: ESA’s Hera Shows Stadium‑Sized Crater on DART‑Hit Dimorphos
close_up_images_reveal_giant_dart_impact.summary: First close‑up images from ESA’s Hera mission reveal a stadium‑wide crater and chaotic tumble on Dimorphos after NASA’s 2022 DART impact.
highlights: The impact created a crater spanning the 151‑m asteroid’s entire width.
Dimorphos now tumbles chaotically in its orbit around 730‑m Didymos.
Hera is flying 30‑25 km from the binary pair at ~12 cm/s using 12 instruments.
CubeSats will be deployed in January to capture even higher‑resolution views.

ai_protein_insulin.headline: AI‑Designed Protein RF‑409 Restores Function of Defective Insulin Receptors
ai_protein_insulin.summary: An AI‑engineered protein called RF‑409 reactivated mutated insulin receptors in mice, lowering blood sugar and protecting pancreatic tissue despite severe insulin resistance.
highlights: RF‑409 lowered blood glucose by ~60% in mice with a Donohue‑syndrome mutation within two hours
The protein’s bloodstream half‑life is about 60‑fold longer than insulin
Treated mice maintained body weight and showed reduced pancreatic damage after 14 days

human_tooth_branch.headline: Ancient Tooth from Southern China May Reveal New Human Lineage
human_tooth_branch.summary: A 100,000‑year‑old tooth uncovered in Guangxi shows protein signatures unlike known Denisovan or Homo sapiens specimens, hinting at a distinct archaic Homo branch.
highlights: Tooth from Chuanshandong dates to at least 100,800 years ago and displays a unique enamel proteome.
Protein variants link the specimen to Homo erectus and Homo antecessor, not to known Denisovan groups.
Uranium-series dating places two Longchuandong teeth between 104,500 and 42,600 years old.
Study appears in Nature and is based on analyses by Qiaomei Fu’s team at the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

hera_spacecraft_gets_1st_up_close_look_a.headline: Hera Reveals Stadium‑Sized Crater on Dimorphos After DART Impact
hera_spacecraft_gets_1st_up_close_look_a.summary: ESA’s Hera spacecraft captured the first close‑up of Dimorphos, showing a stadium‑sized crater and chaotic tumble caused by NASA’s 2022 DART impact.
highlights: The impact created a crater spanning the moonlet’s entire width, comparable to a sports stadium.
Dimorphos is now tumbling wildly, with hundreds of meter‑scale boulders orbiting the binary system.
Hera will approach within 13 km and release two CubeSats—Juventas and Milani—to probe the interior and dust environment.

dna_quantum_sensor.headline: DNA‑Based Quantum Sensors Promise Radio‑Wave Bioimaging Breakthrough
dna_quantum_sensor.summary: Researchers at Technical University of Munich have created DNA nanostructures that fluoresce under magnetic resonance, enabling radio‑wave imaging of molecular processes in tissues.
highlights: Flavin fluorophores in the DNA strands emit fluorescence when local magnetic fields are applied.
Optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) revealed that radio frequency excitation can alter the flavin’s chemical state.
A hairpin‑shaped switch opens upon binding target DNA, activating spin‑enhanced sensing for targeted drug delivery.
DNA nanotechnology allows precise three‑dimensional placement of spins, surpassing the random distribution of nitrogen‑vacancy

alma_reveals_a_dying_star_s_final_breath.headline: ALMA Captures Final Thermal Pulse of Dying Carbon Star IRAS 06530‑0213
alma_reveals_a_dying_star_s_final_breath.summary: Using ALMA, astronomers imaged a giant gas ring from the last thermal pulse of the carbon‑rich preplanetary nebula IRAS 06530‑0213, revealing its recent transition.
highlights: An extended circular ring marks the star’s final thermal pulse about 6,500 years ago.
Mass‑loss rate dropped for ~2,000 years then rose again ~1,000 years before the post‑AGB phase.
The central bipolar nebula and torus indicate a rapid transition to post‑AGB status only ~700 years ago.
Isotopic enrichment in 13C, 17O and 15N challenges standard nucleosynthesis models.

acoustic_priors_cmb.headline: New Acoustic Priors Sharpen Cosmic Microwave Background Constraints
acoustic_priors_cmb.summary: Researchers separate early‑Universe acoustic signals from lensing and ISW effects, delivering tighter CMB measurements of the angular acoustic scale and matter densities.
highlights: Angular acoustic scale measured as 100θ = 1.04100 ± 0.00021.
Physical baryon density ω_b = (2.2440 ± 0.0099) × 10⁻² and ω_bc = 0.1410 ± 0.0011.
Lens‑reconstructed spectrum shows excess features near L≈50 and L≈10³, reduced when WMAP replaces Planck spectra.
Adding ACT DR6 raises ω_b and primordial tilt n_s compared to Planck PR4 alone.
Marginalizing lensing smoothing cuts CMB+DESI preference for w₀wₐCDM over ΛCDM from 3σ to ~2σ.

stage_binary_black_hole_mergers.headline: StAGE Links Binary Black Hole Mergers to Quiescent Galaxy Ancestors
stage_binary_black_hole_mergers.summary: Using the StAGE framework, researchers predict that most binary black hole mergers originate in moderately sub‑solar metallicity stars and later reside in massive quiescent galaxies.
highlights: Most BBH progenitors form at metallicities Z≲Z⊙/3.
Merger‑time hosts have stellar masses 10^{10}–10^{11.5} M⊙ and lie on the star‑forming main sequence at z≈2.
Predicted local BBH merger rates exceed LVK‑inferred ranges for isolated binary models.
Dynamical formation in clusters extends the BBH primary‑mass distribution to high masses.
The stochastic GW background approaches the sensitivity of upcoming LVK upgrades and the Einstein Telescope.

mass_spectral_evidence_iron_sulfate_venu.headline: Iron Sulfate Detected in Venus Cloud Aerosols by Pioneer Venus Probe
mass_spectral_evidence_iron_sulfate_venu.summary: Mass spectra from the Pioneer Venus Large Probe reveal abundant iron sulfates, including hydronium jarosite, in cloud particles near 48‑51 km altitude.
highlights: LNMS detected iron ions (54Fe+, 56FeO+, 54FeO+, 56Fe2O+, 56Fe2O2+) and decomposition gases at ~23 km.
Quantified bulk iron at 0.8 ± 0.4 mg m⁻³ and hydronium jarosite at 2.2 ± 1.2 mg m⁻³ (≈30 wt%).
Iron likely supplied by cosmic dust, requiring only ~2.4 ± 1.5 Myr to accumulate.
Thermal release profiles match decomposition of ferric sulfates releasing Fe2O3, SO2, O2, SO3, H2SO4, and H2O.

arxiv_2611_33815v1.headline: Collisions Trigger Complex Neutrino Flavor Patterns in Astrophysical Gases
arxiv_2611_33815v1.summary: New simulations show that incoherent collisions drive distinct angular and spatial flavor conversions, producing swaps and equipartition while limiting inhomogeneity in dense neutrino gases.
highlights: Linear stability analysis reveals contrasting wavenumber dependences for near‑gapless and far‑gapped branches
Maximum growth rates occur at collision‑scale and collective‑scale wavenumbers respectively
Nonlinear quantum‑kinetic evolution creates flavor swap, equipartition, and secondary growth as the background evolves
Collisional decoherence suppresses spatial inhomogeneities, keeping neutrino populations nearly homogeneous

light_cone_21cm_statistics.headline: Evolving Power Spectrum Sharpens Epoch of Reionization 21‑cm Parameter Estimates
light_cone_21cm_statistics.summary: The evolving power spectrum captures line‑of‑sight evolution, delivering up to three‑fold tighter constraints on reionization parameters compared with traditional cylindrical power spectra.
highlights: Evolving power spectrum (ePS) recovers benchmark 1D‑PS across all scales and redshifts
Artificial neural network emulators trained on 500 light‑cone simulations enable fast inference
SKA‑Low system noise and cosmic variance from 50 realizations incorporated for realistic forecasts
ePS yields credible intervals ~3× tighter than cylindrical PS and ~1.4× tighter than slice‑wise PS

time_frequency_modeling_of_the_lisa_resp.headline: New Time‑Frequency Model Accurately Simulates LISA Response with 10⁻⁹ Mismatch
time_frequency_modeling_of_the_lisa_resp.summary: A vectorized WDM‑based model implemented in JAX reproduces the LISA one‑arm response in the time‑frequency domain with mismatches around 10⁻⁹.
highlights: Uses the Wilson‑Daubechies‑Meyer transformation to represent LISA signals directly in time‑frequency space
Vectorized implementation in JAX enables batch processing of many waveforms
Achieves white‑noise mismatches of ~10⁻⁹ compared with existing LISA response codes

ai_supercomputers_milky_way_simulation.headline: AI-Boosted Triple Supercomputer Simulation Resolves Milky Way Star‑by‑Star
ai_supercomputers_milky_way_simulation.summary: Researchers combined three exascale supercomputers with an AI surrogate to model the Milky Way at individual‑star resolution, using 5.4 trillion particles.
highlights: The simulation employed 5.4 trillion one‑solar‑mass particles, a ten‑fold increase over previous models
AI model PHEASANT predicts supernova‑driven gas evolution, allowing much larger time steps
Three exascale systems—Aurora, Frontier, and JUPITER—ran a unified code across Intel, NVIDIA, and AMD hardware
Lead author Keiya Hirashima of RIKEN presented the results at SC26, a peer‑reviewed conference paper

rift_o4_2026.headline: RIFT Upgrade Enhances Gravitational‑Wave Inference for O4 Observations
rift_o4_2026.summary: The revised RIFT algorithm adds calibration marginalization, new spin coordinates, and automated waveform checks, boosting accuracy and speed for single-event analysis in the O4 run.
highlights: Calibration marginalization now integrated into RIFT’s likelihood framework
New transverse spin and eccentric mean anomaly coordinates improve handling of subtle parameter correlations
Automated waveform symmetry checks catch model regressions before they bias results
Revised operating points optimized for the loudest, clearest O4 signals

the_closest_exoplanets_may_host_magnetic.headline: Magnetic Fields Detected Around Proxima’s Closest Rocky Exoplanets
the_closest_exoplanets_may_host_magnetic.summary: A 2026 Astronomy & Astrophysics study using 117 ESPRESSO observations finds evidence that Proxima Centauri b and d may possess magnetic fields up to dozens of gauss.
highlights: Proxima Centauri d’s field estimated between 8 – 230 gauss, median ~16 gauss, ~27 times Earth’s field
Low‑energy flares repeat with a 5.1‑day period matching Proxima d’s orbit
Statistical analysis shows flares are non‑randomly distributed, suggesting magnetic star‑planet interaction

subsolargw_sn2025adtq_2026.headline: Radio‑silent Type IIb Supernova Challenges Engine‑driven Models for Sub‑solar‑mass Gravitational‑wave Events
subsolargw_sn2025adtq_2026.summary: Deep VLA observations show SN 2025adtq lacks the radio emission seen in SN 2025ulz, questioning jet‑driven superkilonova scenarios for sub‑solar‑mass mergers.
highlights: SN 2025adtq was undetected at 6‑10 GHz to a 3σ limit of ~7.8 µJy, ten times fainter than SN 2025ulz
The non‑detection rules out jet models that remained viable for the earlier radio‑loud counterpart
Observations were conducted with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array under the JAGWAR program 139‑216 days after the GW trigger

345_million_year_old_fossil_reinterprete.headline: Ancient 'Lizzie' Fossil Revealed as Aquatic Stem Tetrapod, Not Early Reptile
345_million_year_old_fossil_reinterprete.summary: Advanced synchrotron X‑ray scans show the 345‑million‑year‑old Westlothiana lizziae possessed gills and thousands of tiny teeth, indicating an aquatic or amphibious lifestyle.
highlights: X‑ray imaging at the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility uncovered internal gills and a fish‑like mouth in the fossil.
The specimen, long considered the earliest amniote, is now placed among stem tetrapods.
Traits such as claws and five‑digit limbs likely evolved in water‑bound ancestors before true land colonization.
The study, published in Nature, prompts reevaluation of Devonian trackway interpretations.

engineered_molecular_glue_egg_chromosome.headline: Engineered Molecular Glue Restores Chromosome Cohesion in Aging Mouse Eggs
engineered_molecular_glue_egg_chromosome.summary: A protein system called TALhesins repaired chromosome connections in older mouse oocytes, boosting proper chromatid pairing from 47% to 74% in a Science paper.
highlights: TALhesins attach to DNA near chromosome centers and release only after fertilization
Proportion of eggs with intact cohesion rose to 74%, matching young mice
The system was engineered by the Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences in Göttingen
Researchers are adapting the approach for human oocytes and have launched a startup, Ovo Labs

chang_e6_spa_samples.headline: Chang'e-6 Samples Pinpoint Ages of Moon’s Largest Impact Basin
chang_e6_spa_samples.summary: Analysis of Chang'e-6 returned material and Chang'e-4 rover data shows the South Pole‑Aitken basin formed 4.34 billion years ago, refining its age.
highlights: South Pole‑Aitken basin dated to 4.34 billion years, narrowing previous 4.35‑4.2 billion‑year range
Apollo basin age determined at 4.2 billion years using magnesium‑rich rock signatures
Computer simulations combined with ~2 kg of returned samples reconstructed a multi‑impact timeline
Findings support the Nice model by linking impact spikes to early giant‑planet migrations

screen_time_vulnerable_ages.headline: Infancy and School Entry Mark Critical Windows for Screen‑Time Impact
screen_time_vulnerable_ages.summary: A longitudinal study of 502 Singaporean children finds that higher screen exposure at age 1 and age 6 predicts lower academic scores and weaker working memory later.
highlights: Screen viewing at age 1 showed the strongest negative association with later academic achievement.
Screen exposure around age 6, when formal schooling begins, also linked to poorer working memory.
Overall cumulative screen time correlated with reduced academic performance across the cohort.
The study tracked screen habits at six intervals from infancy to age 8, using parental reports.

titanium_oxide_gas_detection.headline: Titanium Oxide Gas Detected Around Young Star Orion Source I
titanium_oxide_gas_detection.summary: Astronomers have identified gaseous titanium oxide near the protostar Orion Source I, offering a direct view of rock vaporization at solar system birth.
highlights: First detection of titanium oxide in gas form around a massive protostar
Observations made with high‑resolution spectroscopy at the base of Orion Source I’s outflow
Provides empirical evidence for high‑temperature rocky seeds predicted in planet‑formation models
Builds on earlier 2019 discovery of salty compounds in the same system

invisible_ultrasound_tube_transports_liq.headline: Ultrasonic ‘Invisible Pipe’ Moves Liquids Through Air Without Contact
invisible_ultrasound_tube_transports_liq.summary: Researchers at the University of Helsinki have created an ultrasonic tube that transports liquids and other materials through mid‑air using a programmable acoustic field.
highlights: Elongated Bessel acoustic fields generated by a 256‑speaker array form a stable, tube‑like path in mid‑air
The tube operates at ~40 kHz, consumes about 50 W, and can convey liquids, solids, gases and aerosols without physical walls
The method extends acoustic levitation from single particles to continuous flows, enabling contact‑free dosing and analysis
Published in PNAS, the technique promises applications in handling corrosive, viscous or hazardous fluids

historic_coastal_flooding_california.headline: Super El Niño Fuels Record King Tides Flooding Southern California Coast
historic_coastal_flooding_california.summary: Historic king tides amplified by a super El Niño and a Kelvin Wave inundated Huntington Beach and neighboring communities during Thanksgiving week.
highlights: King tides peaked at 8.19 feet above average low tide in Los Angeles, tying a record set a month earlier.
The Kelvin Wave pushed warm Pacific water northward, intensifying sea‑level rise along the West Coast.
Residents resorted to DIY plywood reinforcements and 300 sand bags as municipal sea‑wall upgrades lag behind.
Long Beach’s $125 million sea‑wall retrofit remains delayed due to budget shortfalls.

stem_cells_alzheimers_trial.headline: World‑First Stem‑Cell Injection Shows Safety and Cognitive Gains in Alzheimer’s Patients
stem_cells_alzheimers_trial.summary: A Phase 1 trial of RBI’s RB‑ADSC therapy demonstrated safety and early cognitive improvement in five Alzheimer’s patients, prompting fast‑track FDA approval for Phase 2.
highlights: Safety confirmed in all five participants
Four of five showed measurable cognitive improvement
Therapy delivers autologous stem cells directly to brain ventricles
Wnt‑protein ‘supercharging’ aims to reduce amyloid‑beta and tau

evt_87762b8fc8.headline: Dogs may hold surprising clues to human longevity
